::: {.callout-important}
## Nothing on this page works yet

There is no release, no image on `ghcr.io` and no `recueil` binary. Every command below is written
in the present tense because that is how a manual reads, but each one is a **Phase 1 or later**
commitment. The Phase column in [the roadmap](roadmap.qmd) says when.

What you *can* do today: read [CONCEPT.md](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONCEPT.md),
read the [concepts](concepts.qmd) page, read the [decision records](adr.qmd), and disagree with any
of it in an issue.
:::

## Choosing a shape

Recueil is one server. How you run it is the only real decision, and it can be changed later
because both shapes run identical code.

| Shape | For | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| **Docker** | A homelab, a NAS, a VPS. The server plus optional sidecars, reachable from every device on your network. | 1 |
| **Desktop** | One machine, no infrastructure. The Tauri shell bundles the same server as a sidecar process on `localhost`. | 4 |
| **From source** | Development, and anyone who prefers it. `pnpm install && pnpm build`. | 1 |

Nothing else needs to be running first. v1 is SQLite only, so there is no database server to
install, and the file is created on first start.

## Docker quickstart

```sh
mkdir -p recueil/{data,storage} && cd recueil
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml
docker compose up -d
```

The server comes up on port 8080 with an empty library. Confirm it:

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:8080/health
```

```json
{"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0","database":"sqlite","items":0}
```

That response on an empty library is the exit criterion for Phase 0, and the first thing that will
be true of this project.

## First run

1. **Create an API token.** Everything authenticates, including the browser session, and everything
   is attributable in the audit log. `recueil token create --name laptop --scope 'items:*'`, or the
   equivalent in Settings.
2. **Point the connector at your server.** Install the Zotero Connector and set its server address
   to your Recueil instance. Recueil speaks the Zotero connector protocol, so the existing extension
   and its roughly six hundred translators work without modification ([ADR-0006](adr.qmd)).
3. **Save something.** Open a paper in the browser and press the connector button. The item, its
   PDF and its metadata land in the library, the PDF is hashed, and enrichment resolves the DOI.
4. **Check that it can leave again.** `recueil export --format bibtex --collection Inbox > inbox.bib`.
   If your data cannot get out on day one, do not put it in.

## Importing an existing library

### From Zotero

The Zotero importer is first-class and is the reason Phase 1 exists.

```sh
recueil import zotero \
  --data-dir ~/Zotero \
  --better-bibtex ~/Zotero/better-bibtex.sqlite \
  --report zotero-import-report.md
```

It reads `zotero.sqlite` directly — items, fields, creators, collections, tags, notes, relations,
imported and linked attachments, annotations and citation keys — hashes every attachment from the
storage directory or a WebDAV archive, and writes a verification report: counts per item type,
attachment hash coverage, and every file it could not find, with the reason.

The run is idempotent, so re-running it after fixing a problem does not duplicate anything, and
Zotero item keys are kept as external identifiers. **Keep Zotero installed and read-only until the
report satisfies you.**

### From Paperless-ngx

```sh
recueil import paperless --url https://paperless.example --token "$PAPERLESS_TOKEN"
```

Documents, tags, correspondents, document types, custom fields, archive serial numbers and the
original files, mapped onto the [Office facet](concepts.qmd#facets). Phase 2.

### From files

BibTeX and BibLaTeX (including `file` fields), RIS, EndNote XML, CSL-JSON, JabRef with groups,
Mendeley exports, and CSV with a column mapping. Every importer has a matching exporter, because a
format you can only read is a trap.
